chunks: From him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from some of his companions, from some of the truthful ones عليهم السلام, who said:
A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and confessed to theft. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn said to him: “Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah?”
He said: “Yes, Sūrat al-Baqarah.” He said: “I have granted your hand to Sūrat al-Baqarah.”

He said: Then al-Ashʿath said: “Are you suspending a hadd from the limits of Allah?” So he said: “And what makes you know what this is? When the proof is established, it is not for the Imam to pardon; but when a man confesses against himself, then that is up to the Imam: if he wishes, he pardons, and if he wishes, he cuts.”

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the act of theft confessed by the man
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the authority exercising judgment
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the legal limits and prescribed penalties set by Allah
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْبَقَرَةِ: Sūrat al-Baqarah, mentioned by the man as what he recites
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, referring to the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: When can the Imam pardon a confessed theft according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a case in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام dealt with a confession of theft and clarified an important legal distinction. It states that when theft is proven by evidence, the Imam does not pardon, but when the accused confesses against himself, the matter is left to the Imam's discretion.
